exercise.name: Knee Plank
steps: Rest on your forearms and knees, elbows under your shoulders.
Make a straight line from your head to your knees and squeeze your stomach.
Breathe steadily and hold for the time.
exercise.one_line_summary: A hold (one picture): face down on the forearms (elbows under the shoulders, forearms parallel) and knees, shins resting on the floor; head, shoulders, hips and knees in one straight line sloping ~17 deg. The beginner regression of the forearm plank; rectus abdominis is the target.

setup.target: Elbows directly under the shoulders, forearms parallel on the floor, fists or palms down.
setup.tolerance: elbow within 0.05 m of under the shoulder
setup.why: NASM forearm plank set-up; library step 1.

setup.target: Knees on the floor about hip-width, shins resting on the floor behind, tops of the feet down.
setup.tolerance: knee contact; feet may be down or lifted
setup.why: NASM knee plank: straight line from head through the knees.

setup.target: Head, shoulders, hips and knees in one straight line; ribs down, glutes squeezed.
setup.tolerance: hip within 0.03 m of the shoulder-knee line
setup.why: NASM cues; no sag, no pike.

movement.measure: root rot X; 90 = flat face-down; 73.3 = body sloping up 16.7 deg to the shoulders
upper arm vertical (elev 73.3, plane 90 in the torso frame)

movement.path: Held; forearm flat on the floor.

muscles.emg: Front plank (toes) RA 46% (IQR 26-61) of peak, 48% with bracing (S2, chronic low-back-pain patients); the knee version is a lower-load regression (S1); long-lever / longer planks raise RA further (S3).
muscles.surface: Vertical bands down the front of the belly.

muscles.emg: EO 77% (60-97) in the braced front plank (S2).
muscles.role: Brace the trunk. Not lit: the library lists abs only; with no study of the knee version, the plank's purpose (abs) wins the single lit slot.
Hold the shoulders over the elbows.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: The belly drops below the shoulder-knee line.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Loads the low back instead of the abs (NASM).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Hips pushed up above the line.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Takes the load off the abs (NASM).

sources.citation: National Academy of Sports Medicine. The plank: coaching, progressions and variations for every client (NASM blog).
sources.what_it_gave: Elbows under shoulders, forearms parallel, straight line; knee plank = straight line head through knees, beginner regression; mistakes sag/pike.

sources.what_it_gave: Front plank RA 46%, braced RA 48% / EO 77% (normalised to session peak); lateral knee plank tested.

Knees and shins on the floor

clip_check.target: hip within 0.03 m of the line
